test_title: PYST 67: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 27 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following ministries announced the fourth phase of amalgamation of RRBs in April 2025 under the 'One State, One RRB' policy to enhance the operational efficiency of regional rural banks (RRBs)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Finance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Finance** has officially set the stage for the **fourth phase** of **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) amalgamation**, which is scheduled to commence in **April 2025**.
 
• This initiative is driven by the **'One State, One RRB'** policy, aiming to consolidate multiple **RRBs** operating within the same state into a single, robust entity to reduce administrative overheads.
 
• The primary objective of this reorganization is to **enhance operational efficiency**, improve **cost-to-income ratios**, and leverage **economies of scale** to better serve the rural population.
 
• Under this plan, the total number of **RRBs** in **India** is projected to be reduced from the existing **43** to approximately **28**, ensuring a more streamlined banking structure.
 
• The **Department of Financial Services (DFS)**, under the **Ministry of Finance**, is the nodal agency coordinating with **Sponsor Banks** and **State Governments** to finalize the roadmap for this consolidation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History of RRBs**: **Regional Rural Banks** were established under the provisions of an Ordinance passed in **September 1975** and the **RRB Act of 1976**, following the recommendations of the **Narasimham Committee**. The first **RRB**, **Prathama Bank**, was established on **October 2, 1975**.
 
• **Shareholding Pattern**: The equity of an **RRB** is held by three parties in a fixed proportion: the **Central Government (50%)**, the **Sponsor Bank (35%)**, and the concerned **State Government (15%)**.
 
• **Phases of Consolidation**: 
 
 
• **Phase 1 (2005)**: Amalgamation of **RRBs** sponsored by the same bank within a state.
 
• **Phase 2 (2012)**: Amalgamation of **RRBs** across different sponsor banks within a state.
 
• **Phase 3 (2019)**: Further consolidation reduced the count to **43** to improve financial viability.
 
 
 
• **Regulation and Supervision**: While **RRBs** are regulated by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, their supervisory powers are vested in the **National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)**.
 
• **Mandate**: **RRBs** are required to provide **75%** of their total credit to the **Priority Sector Lending (PSL)** categories, which is higher than the **40%** requirement for **Scheduled Commercial Banks**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Operational Efficiency**: The **'One State, One RRB'** model helps in **technology integration** and uniform **banking practices** across the state, making it easier for the **Sponsor Banks** to manage operations.
 
• **Financial Health**: Consolidation often leads to better **Capital to Risk-weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR)** and helps weaker **RRBs** benefit from the financial strength of stronger ones within the same geography.
 
• **Geographic Presence**: Despite the reduction in the total number of banks, the **branch network** in **rural** and **semi-urban** areas remains intact or expands, ensuring that **financial inclusion** goals are not compromised.
</ul
